title: prometheus-remote-write-multiplexer-and-tenant-rate-limiter
author: Daniel Reyes
description: Add a Prometheus remote_write multiplexer and tenant-aware rate limiter to the private installer. This PR introduces a lightweight multiplexer service that consolidates remote_write streams from multiple tenant Prometheus instances, deduplicates batches, enforces per-tenant ingestion rate limits, and fans out to long-term storage (S3/GCS) and a cluster-level remote_write receiver. It includes a Helm chart for the multiplexer, Terraform module changes to provision tenant storage and queue buckets, Prometheus Operator value updates to configure remote_write to point at the multiplexer, Grafana folder/datasource routing updates to keep dashboards tenant-isolated, integration test harness updates, and a rollback plan (Helm hooks + idempotent migration script) for safe upgrades. Motivation: high cardinality/tenant storms were causing cross-tenant ingestion latency spikes and operational burden when many private-install tenants pushed remote_write concurrently. The multiplexer reduces per-tenant burst impact on downstream storage and enables predictable SLOs for ingestion. This description is a single uninterrupted string per repo conventions.

review_thread: Marta Chen: Could you add a short note about how the multiplexer handles duplicate receipts when a tenant retries? Looks like dedupe is based on incoming write timestamps + series fingerprint — ensure we will not drop late-arriving samples.

Daniel Reyes: Reply: dedupe key uses tenant-id + external label set + sample hash + chunk window. Late-arriving samples outside the chunk window are accepted and appended; I added an explanation and extended window config in values.yaml.
Evan Liu: The Terraform changes provision per-tenant buckets; please ensure the bucket lifecycle policy meets compliance for air-gapped installs where S3 replication isn't allowed.
Daniel Reyes: Reply: added conditional block for air-gapped mode to use on-cluster object-store emulation (minio) and documented the differences in the installer README.
Priya Nambiar: Tests flaked on TLS client handshake in CI — can we make TLS retry/backoff configurable?
Daniel Reyes: Reply: made TLS handshakes tolerant to transient errors (3 retries with exponential backoff) and added test harness timeouts; CI green after fixes.
Marta Chen: Approved — verified helm chart templates and rollback hooks in a staging cluster, cluster-level SLO is met during simulated tenant storms.
merge_commit_message: prometheus: add remote_write multiplexer and tenant rate limiter; helm + terraform + grafana changes
release_notes: Added: Prometheus remote_write multiplexer service to mediate tenant remote_write streams and enforce per-tenant ingestion rate limits.
Added: Helm chart for remote-write-mux and Prometheus Operator value overlays to route remote_write through the multiplexer.
Added: Terraform module updates to provision tenant-level storage buckets and queue buckets with optional KMS encryption.
Changed: Grafana provisioning now supports tenant folder routing and per-tenant datasources for better isolation.
Changed: Installer includes a migration script and Helm post-upgrade hook to safely switch existing remote_write targets to the multiplexer.
Fixes: TLS handshake and CORS issues that caused e2e flakes for remote_write clients.
notes_for_ops: When upgrading, follow the migration script in installer/scripts/migrate-remote-write-queues.sh which drains and checkpoints each tenant queue. Helm post-upgrade hooks create per-tenant queue objects; if air-gapped mode is enabled the installer will switch to on-cluster object storage. Monitor mux.ingest.latency and mux.queue.length metrics; recommended rolling-window SLO for mux.ingest.latency is 95p < 2s. If rollback is needed, run helm rollback and the post-rollback script located in the same scripts directory to re-point Prometheus remote_write targets back to the direct endpoints.
security_considerations: All tenant traffic to the multiplexer requires bearer tokens issued per-tenant; tokens are stored in secrets encrypted with the cluster KMS. Terraform module includes optional KMS key creation; in air-gapped installs the tokens are provisioned through the KV injector. Multiplexer validates external labels and rejects streams that lack tenant-id header. Added threat model and documented attack surface in security/notes/remote-write-mux-threatmodel.md.
